utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue with Dr. Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just prior to bringing the witness in, there is one matter I would like to raise in connection with Mr. Niemann's comments before the court yesterday. The particular circumstance that led us to raise this issue was that it is our understanding that there have been public comments either through representatives of the Defence or, perhaps, relatives of the accused that an issue the Defence may raise is the issue of a mistake of identity, in that there may have been another man who looked very much like the accused. That was the concern that prompted us to raise this issue because if, in fact, that is correct, and the Defence chooses to go forward with that issue in their case in-chief without asking our witnesses about it, then we would be compelled to attempt to bring our witnesses back to address that issue because of concerns that we have raised here with the Chamber as well as time concerns and the impact on the witnesses being brought back for such a matter. We raise this question to the court of how we should proceed on that. The witness that is before the Tribunal now would be such a witness that we would either deal with that issue on direct or if the Defence were going to deal with it on cross-examination. So, that is the particular issue that we had in mind when we raised the question. There is a bit of immediacy to that. I suppose one or two witnesses we could attempt to recall, but I wanted again to raise that specific issue with the court so they would have a better understanding of why we raised the concern at the time we did.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Do you have anything to add, Mr. Kay?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. The challenge to the witness which we are now discussing, Mr. Q, was on the basis that he did not see what he alleged he saw, and that case was quite clearly put to that witness, as the court may recollect, yesterday in relation to his allegation against the defendant. In those circumstances, the Defence has discharged its obligation to cross-examine on an issue with which it was in disagreement with the witness, and that would fall squarely within the rules, as I understand them, from my jurisdiction and other jurisdictions that apply the same criteria. The court may, perhaps, need some time to look at the transcripts of what actually took place yesterday and on the late afternoon of Tuesday but, as I understood it, it was quite clear that that witness was challenged in relation to his allegations.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Are you making a reference to a specific witness or is this a general issue?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would, I believe, be a potential issue with the present witness, Dr. Blazevic. We clearly understood the import of the Defence cross-examination with Q and we understand that is not the issue here, but we believe there may be other witnesses that this would be the same issue.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I got the impression that the two of you were like two ships passing in the night, you were at cross-purposes, so you are referring to the present witness and as a general proposition. It may be something that we need to take up in camera by way of a discussion of the meaning of Rule 67A(ii)(b) which requires that the Defence shall notify the Prosecutor of its intent to offer any special defence and then it goes on. It says, "including that of diminished or lack of mental responsibility", and I can recall at one of our in camera pretrial conferences there was a discussion about what else did that rule entail. I do not know whether there is a possibility that that rule entails what we are talking about now. I received just this morning something from Blackstone's Criminal Practice that came from the Prosecutor, I understand -- at least, one of the law clerks said that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I see also there is something from Australian Evidence Ligertwood. That is it. Does the Prosecutor intend to offer anything else on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, we could put this into a formal motion, if that would be a more convenient way of dealing with it?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was just wondering if you were wanting to offer anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I merely gave that in support of the matter I raised yesterday. It is just the authority for the proposition I was raising, but if your Honours would be more assisted with it being put into a formal motion, then I certainly would do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: That probably is helpful, particularly since the Defence has indicated at least yesterday that they would probably take a different position.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I am concerned though about this witness. I do not know how much longer you have with this witness, but if this issue is being raised with respect to this witness, it seems to me that there may be a need on the part of the Trial Chamber to resolve this issue quickly. Of course, what we have is information from Blackstone's and Ligertwood, two pages -- five pages, I guess. So, is it your intent, is it your desire, Miss Hollis, for the Trial Chamber to resolve this issue before you conclude with this witness or at least before cross-examination is concluded?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I guess we would have two options perhaps; one option is that the Trial Chamber resolve this. That would be our preferred option. The second option would be if there is no resolution, that we then either in our direct or perhaps be allowed in redirect to ask questions going to this issue, if the Defence does not raise it in their cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You can hear this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes, the terminology is becoming clearer as people express the idea. What I was talking about yesterday was, in fact, on a different matter. "Putting your case" and "cross-examination" are two slightly different issues; cross-examination, challenging those issues of substance that you disagree with in the Prosecution case, and no-one expects you to cross-examine on every single thing under the sun that a witness talks about as, the court would appreciate, we would be here for a long while. "Putting the case", I was understanding entirely something different which is where you assert your case to the witness and say, "Is that not right?" They either deny it or accept it, which is a slightly different procedure looking at the document I have been given this morning. Cross-examination was something that we fully intended to follow within this understanding of our obligation to any court as we would see it, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe in the light of what Defence counsel has just said that solves the issue for us and solves our concerns in the matter.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Thank you, Mr. Kay. Are you ready to call your next witness ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: -- or continue with Dr. Blazevic? DR. AZRA BLAZEVIC, recalled Examined by MISS HOLLIS, continued.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic, you understand you are still under oath, do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, at the conclusion of your testimony yesterday you indicated at some point in the medical centre the soldiers took a woman named Gordana from the medical centre; when she had returned she said they had taken her so she could point out her flat so they would not touch it. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but so that they would not touch her flat. That is how I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, and what was Gordana's ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that once the medical supplies from the medical clinic were loaded on a military vehicle you were taken toward the centre of Kozarac. I would like Prosecution Exhibit 195, a film of Kozarac, to be played showing the hospital again, please? Dr. Blazevic, if you could look carefully at the condition of the hospital as it is shown on this film.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If that film could be removed, please? Dr. Blazevic, as you examined the medical centre as it was shown on that film, did that film depict the basic condition of the medical centre as it appeared when you left it on 26th May 1992? I am speaking of the building itself.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so, that it looked exactly like that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You had mentioned that a shell hit the building and hit a corner of the building. Was that corner of the building shown on that film clip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were taken from the medical centre towards the centre of Kozarac were all the other medical personnel taken with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did these soldiers accompany you as you were moved towards the centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken towards the intersection of Marsala Tita Street, the one which goes through the centre of Kozarac and the old road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did they eventually stop you and the other medical personnel, at what location?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They stopped by the sweet shop, by the pastry shop in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the way between the medical centre and the intersection, I believe you indicated that you were taken there along Marsala Tita Street, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, part of the street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to observe the condition of the buildings as you walked along Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you observe about the condition of the buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were damaged by shells.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you walked along did you smell smoke or see any of the buildings on fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In one part one could see smoke behind, in the rear, behind those houses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you walked along Marsala Tita Street did you pass the home and cafe of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you observe of the condition of the home and cafe of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that glass was broken on the cafe, on the house of -- probably by shells which had been falling because that whole area was rather badly damaged by shells.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you notice anything on the home or cafe of Dule Tadic that appeared as though it had been actually hit by a shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean a direct hit ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- of a shell, no.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you got to this pastry shop what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were told there to stop and wait.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at the pastry shop did you see any people from the convoy that had left earlier that morning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see while you were at this pastry shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could see several groups of soldiers there and a truck parked on the side.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then what happened after you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were standing and waiting, a soldier came and called out one of the members of this medical personnel who was professionally the ambulance car driver, Mohamed Bahonjic, and told him to follow him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, what was the name of the man who was called out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nihad Bahonjic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was he called out? Was he called out by name or otherwise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The soldier approached us and uttered his name and family name and told him to follow him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Nihad Bahonjic, had he been with you at the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had he also been with you at the motel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of Nihad Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The soldier who called out Nihad Bahonjic by name, did you recognise this soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did it appear to you that Nihad recognised this soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after the soldier called Nihad out by name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He took him a little further away from where we were and they remained standing there in the street by a group of soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And as we were waiting there somebody said, "There is Dule".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you heard that what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I looked up, it meant that somebody whom we knew was there. I looked around and I noticed Dusko Tadic crossing the street, not far away.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you saw him crossing the street, what was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was simply crossing the street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And was he carrying anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in one hand he had a kind of a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: With his other hand was he doing anything?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it was raised in the air as if he was saying something to someone, or trying to draw someone's attention.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your memory, what was Dule Tadic wearing when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If Prosecution Exhibit 196, the map of Kozarac, could be placed on the overhead projector, please? If the witness could please point out for the court, first, where she was standing when she saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here, more or less in front of this building here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this would have been the building where the pastry shop was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You are now at the intersection of what some people call the old Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please point out for the court where Dule Tadic was when you saw him and in which direction he was moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was roughly here and he was crossing the street from this side towards the direction of the school.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If I could have this document 7/20 marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: For the record, the witness pointed to where now when she saw him?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: He was at the top of the triangle?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The witness pointed to an area near the road at the top of the triangle, and indicated that the accused was moving across the road toward the school. If this could be marked Prosecution Exhibit 202 for identification, please? (To the witness): If you could please examine that photograph? That is document 7/20. Dr. Blazevic, do you recognise that as the intersection you were just referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Does it show the shop that was the pastry shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Perhaps, your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 202.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 202 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that photograph could be placed on the overhead projector, please? (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, if you could use the pointer and help orient the court for this photograph, would you please point to the area where you said that you were standing when you saw the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be this place here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would be in front of that building on the other side of the intersection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: For our reference purposes, in which direction would Marsala Tita be running toward the mosque?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be this direction.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So as we are looking at the photograph, it would be as the road goes off to the left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it would be the road to the left going by this house and then further through Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then if we look to the right side of the photograph, we see the road coming around that wedge of grass to the right, where would that road be leading?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean this road here?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This road, in this part here turns into two roads, and one goes to the left side towards Kamicani and the other one goes straight towards Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The one that goes towards Kamicani, would that run past the church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The one that goes to the Banja Luka road you are talking about, the new Prijedor/Banja Luka road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The school on this map would be in which direction on this photograph here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The school would be somewhere here, in this part here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So it would be on the -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the left side of the picture that we do not have. We do not have this place here shown.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We do not have the school, but it would be on the left of the picture shown by the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please show the court where it was that you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be approximately here, on this part of the road somewhere here. He was crossing the road from this direction, coming from near the house where at one time there was a technical goods store and he was moving towards the school.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you please show us how far across the road he walked as you watched him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him just for a moment approximately in the part of the road that was probably here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that you saw him walking, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, is that the only area of the road you saw him or did you see him as he moved closer towards the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only saw him walking in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So if you could show again to the court where it was that you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This would be just in front of one of the points on the triangle near where two people are shown walking, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It would be in this part where the two roads join into one road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were then looking across the wedge of grass as you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What time of the day was it that you arrived at the intersection and saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Have you any idea about what time of the afternoon it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell exactly, perhaps around 3 o'clock, maybe later.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was it a sunny day or was it a cloudy day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a sunny day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there anything between you and the accused which obstructed your view of the accused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you able to see him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was just a moment, a few seconds.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there anything about that incident that made your sighting of Dule Tadic stick out in your mind, remain in your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It remained in my mind because Nihad Bahonjic was not taken from that intersection with us to Trnopolje, and all of the time after that we were wondering why was he taken and who took him, because the soldier that came and called out Nihad Bahonjic called him out by his name and last name, none of us knew that soldier and I remember that the only known face -- the only person that we knew and who was there at that time was exactly Dusko Tadic. That is it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated yesterday, just for a matter of clarification for the record, that you believe that you had known Dusko Tadic to see him in passing from the time you began to practise veterinary medicine in Kozarac. Could you tell us please ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: -- when that would have been when you started to practise veterinary medicine in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In July of 1983.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Of 1983 in Kozarac or 1986 when you moved to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I moved into Kozarac a few years later. It was in 1986.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, you would first have known Mr. Tadic in 1983 when you began to practise in Kozarac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that on a weekly basis you would perhaps see Dule Tadic in Kozarac every day, perhaps on occasions several times in one day. Prior to 26th May, when do you last recall seeing Dule Tadic in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly the day, but it was perhaps a day or two before the attack on Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was 26th May the last time you saw Dule Tadic in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this incident at the intersection, were you and the others eventually taken away from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you transported from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the place where we were standing, we were taken to a place on the road to Kozarusa, when you leave Kozarac and go through a new road to Prijedor, we were taken by a jeep or a similar vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was Nihad Bahonjic taken with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he remained there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Have you ever seen Nihad Bahonjic again after that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could the witness please be given Prosecution Exhibit 79? If the photograph could be provided back to the Registrar? Could you look at that map for a moment and then, if we could put it on the overhead projector, if you could show the court the direction that you were taken in the military vehicle and where you were taken in the military vehicle? If that could be put on the overhead projector, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be an intersection of old road where we were standing. We were taken towards the new Banja Luka road, and then we were driving on the new Banja Luka road towards Prijedor, and we came to the place that would be approximately here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. On this route that you have just shown the court, it appears that you went through a portion of Kozarusa or near Kozarusa, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see as you passed through or near Kozarusa? What did you see of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw that all of the village was burnt.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The inhabitants of Kozarusa, to your knowledge, they were what ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This military vehicle took you to what location? Was it to a building or a structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The vehicle stopped in front of a tavern which in Kozarac was known as Zikina tavern.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would appear to be at an intersection that is to the right of "Coralic", the word "Coralic" on the map, and also is below the word "Coralic" on the map, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be a place that can be seen exactly here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Then what happened once you were taken to this cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were stopped there. They told us to leave and we waited here again.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were waiting did you have any guards or escorts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were soldiers there in front of the tavern, soldiers that stood on the road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened then after you had waited there for a time? Where were you taken from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that we were told to enter one of the buses that were standing there and they took us to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This bus that you entered, what type of a bus was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was a plain transportation bus which is normally used in the public transportation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On your route from Kozarac and then to Trnopolje, at any time did you see any combat vehicles such as tanks or amoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember seeing them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time after the Serb takeover of Prijedor and the attack on Kozarac, had you ever seen tanks or amoured personnel carriers either near Kozarac or near Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once I saw a tank in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That tank was in the intersection of new Banja Luka road and the road that crosses from Kozarac in the direction of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was it that you saw that tank at that intersection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not be able to say exactly, but perhaps seven days, maybe more, before the attack on Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were taken to Trnopolje to what location in Trnopolje were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought us to Trnopolje, to the place located near the rail road station and we were told to go to the clinic in Trnopolje, medical clinic in Trnopolje, and stay there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When your bus actually stopped you were near what building in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The bus stopped a little bit further in a meadow from which one could go into the school in Trnopolje, or into the building of -- municipal building in Trnopolje or into the medical clinic in Trnopolje and we were told to go into the medical clinic in Trnopolje and remain there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When this bus arrived in Trnopolje, who met the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many soldiers there and a man whom I did not know at that time, and later I found out that that was Slobodan Kuruzovic, the Commander of the camp in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you did not know him prior to your arrival at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the day that you arrived there and he met you with the soldiers, what were the soldiers wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was Mr. Kuruzovic wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that Mr. Kuruzovic was the Commander of Trnopolje camp. How did you come to learn that he was the Commander of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We found that out because during our later stay in Trnopolje, if we were asking somebody something or requesting something, the guards were always mentioning Commander Kuruzovic. I know that people who wanted to leave the camp or who were leaving the camp, they had to have an authorisation from the Commander, Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Kuruzovic ever give you orders of any type while you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that he told you to go to the medical centre at the camp. Who along with yourself was told to go to the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole group that came from Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That medical centre was located inside the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that medical centre where you worked and slept for the rest of your stay at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I spent in Trnopolje until mid August. I was there until mid August of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time could the next video in line please be shown?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is that 190?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this would be Prosecution Exhibit 203 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Could the video be stopped here, please? (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, do you recognise what is being shown on the video?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is being shown on the video? What is the structure we are looking at here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the building of the elementary school in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The elementary school that was part of the camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 203 for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to Exhibit 203?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 203 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, as we began this tape we saw a fence that was next to a house. If we go forward again, please, we see a fence as it runs along in front of the school. If we can go forward from there? Stop here, please. It appears the fence is broken in parts but then continues to run on, on the other side of the school. Was that fence there in Trnopolje when you arrived at the camp on 26th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the fence was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The portions that are shown where the fence has fallen down, was the fence standing in those areas when you arrived there in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have seen evidence in this court of a barbed wired fence at Trnopolje camp. Do you recall that barbed wire fence being erected at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When was that barbed wired fence erected at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That fence was erected immediately before the inmates from Keraterm and Omarska were transferred to Trnopolje which could be at the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that an estimate on your part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is a fact. I could not say whether between the time when the fence was erected, whether four or five days went by, but not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How long was that fence actually standing at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That fence was there during that period of time until the inmates from Keraterm came and I think that the same night or maybe the next day after they came, the fence was removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: All right. If we could go back to the video, please. This building that we are approaching -- could you stop the video there, please -- this building that we now see, the white building to the left of which is the white vehicle, what is that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The building in the background -- do you mean the building in the background behind the vehicle or the building in front of the picture?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The building in front of the picture, the building to the right of the white UN vehicle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is the building where the store in Trnopolje was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did that building have a back portion to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that back portion where the medical clinic was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could continue the film, please? If we could continue the film, please? If we could stop the film here? Excuse me, if we could back up just a bit, just a few frames? (To the witness): What is this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the building which housed a former Local Commune of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of things were in this building? What types of functions were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean when I was in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, before it was a camp, what was the building normally used for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was a Local Commune or a local government building. I do not know, how should I call this -- local government, a smaller local government unit than opstina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Was there sometimes a cinema in that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was -- a cinema was there in this building in the back of this building that you cannot see from here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could advance the film, please? If we could stop the film here, please? What is this building that we are now seeing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the storage or the store for the building materials.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were detainees ever held in this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which detainees were held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning, this building, the groups were held here for a day, two or three. The group of inmates from Omarska were held here for several days before they joined the rest of the camp of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could continue the film, please? This intersection here and as we are turning towards the intersection, we would be heading in what direction as we turn to the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The building that we see, the side of the building, is this the Local Commune you were speaking of, the long building with the rectangular windows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this would be the movie theatre, the cinema.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In fact, the building with the windows below and above that would be the side of the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could be stopped here, please? We have seen a film of a visit by Penny Marshall and in part of that film she showed tents that were erected in the field next to and behind the school building. Do you recall those tents being erected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that happen, when were those tents erected?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, it was a day or two after Keraterm inmates arrived in Trnopolje, in fact, when this wire fence fell.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who erected those tents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The inmates themselves, trying to make some kind of a makeshift shelter.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of materials did they use to do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Anything they could come by around the area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could continue the film, please? Were there also tents behind the school as it was shown, as it went behind it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the tents stretched towards the school and then behind the school, between the school and the cinema, and next to the cinema.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that film could please be stopped and rewound back to the black portion and I will ask for it later, please. (To the witness): At this time I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 204 for identification and this would be document 40/35. If that could be shown to the witness, please? Do you recognise that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the foreground, one sees the side wall of a shop in Trnopolje and in the background is the part of the building which housed the surgery, the outpatient unit in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be put on the overhead? Your Honour, I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 204?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 204 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As we look at that building and we look at the front portion of the building which is to our left, the white portion, is that the store that you spoke of earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. (Indicated) It is this building here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The back portion of the building is where your medical clinic was located, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you point to the area of that back portion where your medical clinic was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It appears that there are three windows there, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those windows then would have looked into the area that was your medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, these are windows of the corridor which passed by the premises of the medical -- of the outpatient clinic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So your clinic would have been on the other side of the court or where these three windows were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could offer or have this marked as Prosecution Exhibit 205 for identification and shown to be the witness? This will be document 40/29. (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, does that photograph depict the back portion of the store building, the connecting hallway and the building in which the cinema is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would offer Prosecution Exhibit 205.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 205 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that could be placed on the overhead projector, please? (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, looking at this photograph, could you again point out for the court the back part of the store building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This would be the back of the building which houses the shop.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The building or the portion of that building where the medical clinic is located is where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you look at the connecting portion between the store building and the cinema, what was located in that connecting portion that appears red to us here on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean this part here?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In this part was the former laboratory of the outpatient clinic in Trnopolje. Then another room which, as far as I know, belonged to the Local Commune before and that would be all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This laboratory, did you ever use that as a laboratory while you were at the camp in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If that exhibit then could be provided to the Registrar, please? (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, while you were at Trnopolje camp were there guards who guarded the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes there were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These guards who guarded the camp, what did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they carry weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these guards who guarded the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The guards that you knew, where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were either from Prijedor or surroundings, villages around Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The guards that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know how many guards worked at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were very many points, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know how many shifts of guards there were at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean how many groups alternated or how often they changed?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many groups alternated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three or four different groups of guards which alternated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know how long they would work in a shift?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It varied.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there guards who were working at the camp 24 hours a day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to the guards at the camp and to Kuruzovic, the camp Commander, were there other individuals who worked at the camp on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us who these people were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, for instance, Slavko Puharic, who, to our knowledge, was Deputy Commander, and then there were the Red Cross, they came daily.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Red Cross, do you mean the International Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Prijedor Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was in charge of the Red Cross there at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Pero Curguz.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know him from before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did the Serbian or the Prijedor Red Cross do for the detainees at the camp? What services did they provide?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Other individuals who worked at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, were there other individuals who worked at the camp in addition to the ones you have mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Were there other medical individuals who came to the camp and worked there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, there was a physician, Dusko Ivic, and a paramedic, a medical assistant, who was with him and whom they called Mica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This doctor, Dr. Dusko Ivic, did you know him from before the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you get to know him while you were at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you become acquainted with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he would drop by the camp every day. From Dr. Idriz Merdzanic I learnt his name because this was a man whom he knew before and with whom he had worked before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you learn his ethnic group as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said he came to the camp every day. Did this medical assistant, Mica, come to the camp every day as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What medical services did they provide to the detainees at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they tell you what their position was and why they were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Dusko Ivic said that a Crisis Committee in Prijedor had made him responsible for looking after the hygiene and health situation in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have indicated that Kuruzovic had authority to allow people to leave the camp. Did anyone else at Trnopolje camp have the authority to allow detainees to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From time to time the camp could be left with a certificate issued by Dr. Dusko Ivic certifying to the poor state of health of that individual or a certificate issued by the Red Cross in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to the guards in the camp and these personnel that you have just named, while you were in Trnopolje, did others come to the camps, soldiers come into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Trnopolje camp, did these soldiers have any difficulty in getting access into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The soldiers who came to the camp, did you know any of these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you knew, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came from nearby villages.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry I did not hear the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When they came to the camp were they armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated earlier in your testimony that one of the soldiers who came into the medical clinic later visited Trnopolje and you learned his name, Ljubo Stojanovic. How often did Ljubo Stojanovic visit the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him once or maybe twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated when he came to the camp at some point he told you that he was from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall a conversation with him in which conversation he told you he was living in Kozarac at the time he was talking with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he tell you about his living in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that was during this conversation when we talked about where he came from and he said he was from Belgrade, but that he also lived in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he show anything that had an address on it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as I was rather surprised as I knew more or less all people, all the people who lived, at least, in that part of Kozarac which he had mentioned. I said that I could not believe it, that I did not know him, and then he showed me his ID and there was the address.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what part of Kozarac that address indicated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Marsala Tita Street and I do not remember the number.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall where it was located on Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he tried to explain it to me and it should be approximately in the part close to Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, the people who had previously lived in that area near Mutnik mosque, what was the ethnic group of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This identification card he showed you that had his address in Kozarac on it, do you recall the date of that identification card?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it because that was one thing which sounded very odd and we talked about it later, the date was of some four or five days before the attack on Kozarac, I believe it was 19th May.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the camp at Trnopolje, were there any Serb officials who visited the camp there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, once an army officer came to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it, Slobodan Cumba.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know why he visited the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came to the surgery, introduced himself, and said that he was in charge of the security situation in that part of the Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While he was at the medical clinic talking with you, do you recall him making comments about ethnic cleansing taking place in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was very frank and said, well, Kozarac fared as it did because, allegedly, there were extremists there and did not surrender the weapons. Brdo turned over the weaponry and will fare the same; and he also spoke that, had it occurred to somebody to carry -- it had occurred to somebody to carry out ethnic cleansing and that that was what would happen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You mentioned that another area would have the same fate. Did he mention anything about a place called Biscani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he say about Biscani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said: "They returned the weapons over and yet they will suffer the same lot as you".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened to Biscani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Seven days later that area was also cleansed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he was talking with you, he used the term "cleansing"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have looked at the buildings that were part of the camp at Trnopolje. Do you recall, were there structures across the street from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the immediate vicinity of the camp were some private houses, residential houses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did camp personnel ever use those homes for any purposes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which homes were used by camp personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of them was right across the street from Trnopolje school where the army was stationed; why, I do not know. There was also another house which was a little further away from the camp towards Kozarac on the right-hand side, and this was a building which officially housed the premises of Slobodan Kuruzovic, where he worked.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could play the second portion of Prosecution Exhibit 203, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could stop here, please? This structure that has the green awning on it, do you recognise that structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any camp personnel use that structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, during a period of time there was the Red Cross on the one side and on the other side, that is, in the other part of that house, was a post, a duty post, and the military.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What had this house been before, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a private pub.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that at one point the Red Cross used a portion of this house. Where was the Red Cross located before it used this building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the offices of the former Local Commune in Trnopolje, and within the grounds of the camp we could see it on a former, on an earlier picture.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That would have been the building in which you said the cinema was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in the front part.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go forward, please? If we could stop here? This area, was there any sort of use made of this area next to this cafe house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Right where this woman is standing on both sides of the fence was a military checkpoint, a sentry post.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could continue the video, please? If we could stop the film here, please? This two-storey red structure, do you recognise that structure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This brick ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- this building made of bricks? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was that structure used by any of the camp personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a house that Slobodan Kuruzovic used.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could shut off the video, please? Could you tell us during the time that you were at Trnopolje, were there a group of medical personnel who worked in the clinic with you during that entire time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you tell us who those people were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean to list their names?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, the medical personnel who worked with you the entire time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were doctors Idriz Merdzanic, Jusuf Pasic, Mensur, myself, and my colleague, Hase Dzonlagic, and then a veterinary, medical assistant, Mujo Zulic and a nurse, Sabiha Islamovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned Mensur, what was Mensur's last name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kusuran.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did all of these individuals you have named leave Trnopolje with you when you left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were leaving at difference intervals.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were any of them taken from Trnopolje to other camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, two physicians, Dr. Jusuf Pasic and Dr. Mensur Kusuran, were taken to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We have had evidence, as I said, of the Penny Marshall visit. I would ask that a portion of Prosecution Exhibit 184 be played. That was a portion of that visit. It would be the portion showing the medical clinic at Trnopolje. If we could stop that there, please? Can you tell us, please, we are looking at a gentleman here with a white coat on who is missing part of his right arm. Could you tell us who that person is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is a paramedic, Mica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is the paramedic who would come to the camp with Dr. Ivic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The gentleman that is walking toward Mica, that is Dr. Idriz, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could move forward, please? If we could stop it here? This gentleman in the white coat to our left, who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is Vasif Gutic who was also with us in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he a doctor as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a student of medicine and was about to graduate actually.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could now move to the next portion of that tape, the last segment, please? If we could, please, move forward through that to the -- if we could stop there, please? Dr. Blazevic, is this yourself that we are seeing on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were speaking with Penny Marshall at this time, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were you telling her about at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was trying to say that there was a group of people missing because until that moment all the inmates from Keraterm had been transferred to Trnopolje, as far as we knew, and half of the inmates kept at the Omarska camp, and another half was taken from Omarska to a direction which we did not know about, and we had only heard that they had been sent to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During a very short portion of her visit, Penny Marshall was able to speak with you and other medical personnel in private, was she not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During that small portion of time, were you able to speak freely with her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was too afraid.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you think would happen to you if you spoke freely about Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, that they would kill us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who did you think would do that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you like to continue, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, before the break we were talking about the medical personnel who had come to Trnopolje camp with you. Did the woman Gordana also come to the camp with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long was she held at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was at the camp for perhaps 10 days and then after that she was taken home.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who took her home, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She told us that her brother came to pick her up.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this 10 day period or so that Gordana was in Trnopolje camp with you, do you recall any unusual incident in which she may have been involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that once when two men were beaten in the lab premises in Trnopolje, one of them told us that in the room where they were located, one female in a lab coat came in accompanied by two soldiers and they talked about something between them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The women in Trnopolje who wore such lab coats, do you know who these women were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the three of us, myself, Sabiha Zulic and Gordana.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you and Sabiha discuss this information that had been provided to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had you gone into that room when the man was being beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, had Sabiha gone into that room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was the man who told you about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was Nedzad Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you first arrived at Trnopolje camp were there already detainees at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were many people there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the camp, did other people arrive at the camp, other detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the situation in Trnopolje was chaotic at all times. There was a large fluctuation of people. There was a group of maybe 1500 to 2,000 men who were there at all times and, in addition to this, people, civilians, women, children were brought in all the time, and from there they were deported to other places.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the camp, did you know any of these other detainees in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of the detainees in this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were almost all of them Muslim and a couple of Croats.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the relative age groups of the personnel in the camp, the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was quite varied, from 15 or 16 year olds to elderly people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people who were brought into the camp, where did they come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were from surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the Serbs ever say anything as to why these people kept coming into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serbs were always saying that we were there, in fact, so that they could protect us from Muslim extremists.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people coming into the camp from the surrounding villages, what did they tell you as to why they were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They told us they were there because they were brought there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Brought there by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the military.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they tell you what had happened to their villages and their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they say had happened to their villages and their homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The story was almost always -- the story that was repeated was almost always the same. The military would come and order the people to leave their houses in a very short time. Usually, they would kill several people, and the rest of the people were sent to the camp in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These soldiers who came to the villages and ordered the people to leave and kill some of the people, did these detainees tell you that these were Muslim soldiers who did this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What ethnic group were the soldiers who did this, according to the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were Serb soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From the camp could you see fires in the surrounding areas during your time in Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From what areas or villages could you see these fires?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For a long time one could see the fire in the direction of Kozarac, in all of the villages surrounding Kozarac and the hills that were turned towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The villages from which these detainees came, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These areas from which you could see these fires, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of the inhabitants of these areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were held at Trnopolje camp were you ever allowed to leave the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I left the camp several times.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever, in fact, go back to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The first time that you went back, when was that? How many days or so after you had arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was two or three days after I arrived to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you go back to Kozarac on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We asked them to take us at least to the building of the medical centre in Kozarac so that we could try and see whether any medicine were left there, that we could use to help people that were there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had military accompany us to the Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you arrived at Kozarac, the area of the town that you could see, did the condition of the town appear any different than when you had been taken from it on 26th May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not significantly changed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your second visit then back to Kozarac, when did that occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It took place perhaps at the end of June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this second trip to Kozarac why did you go there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We wanted actually to try and retrieve the documents, our documents, our personal documents, that seemed very important to us at that time, and none of us took any of those documents with us before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this second occasion how did you get from Trnopolje camp to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you took a bicycle from the camp to Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we came close to Kozarac on a bicycle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then when you were close to Kozarac did you then have an escort for the rest of your trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This escort, you got the escort at what point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I came on a bicycle to the place on the road between Kozarac and Trnopolje which is quite close to the intersection with the new Banja Luka road that we used to call "Suhi Brod".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it at that point that you had the escort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This escort, was this escort one of a group of soldiers who were at this point?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of the soldiers was present on that road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were actually able to go into Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far were you able to walk in Kozarac on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that day I went on foot through Kozarac and I reached Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this second trip to Kozarac was the condition of the buildings in the town significantly different than your earlier trip?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that time, at that time Kozarac was completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say that Kozarac was "completely destroyed", did you see any buildings in the town that appeared to be relatively undamaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What buildings were those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were mostly the houses of the Serbs that were along that road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
