utterances.text: Along Marsala Tita?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on Marsala Tita Street and on another street that leads towards -- that leads from the orthodox church to the medical centre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These homes, the Serb homes, that were undamaged, did you know the owners of these homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were these Serb owners?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On that street I saw the house of Bozo Dragicevic, the house of Dusko Tadic, the house of Drago Coprka, Mirko Grahovac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These houses were all relatively undamaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any of these houses you have just mentioned have signs on them or writing of any kind on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was quite typical for those -- all of those houses to have a sign that explained that the house belonged to the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the houses you have mentioned, for example, Bozo Dragicevic, did you see such a sign on his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what that sign said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would say either "This is Serbian" or "This is" -- or it would say "This is a Serbian house", but mostly "This is Serbian".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the house and cafe of Dusko Tadic, did you see such a sign?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it said, it was written on one side, I do not recall from which side, "A Serb house, do not touch".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The other two houses that you mentioned, Grahovac and the other gentleman, did those two houses have signs on them as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the house of Mirko Grahovac, there was a drawing, a typical drawing, of Serbian cross with four S’s, and on the house of Drago Coprka, there was a big Serb flag.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Again when you say the four S’s, you are talking about the four Cyrillic S’s?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it correct that in the normal alphabet or the Latin alphabet, these Cyrillic S’s would somewhat resemble the letter "C"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned those four houses that were not destroyed. Did you also have occasion to see the Serb church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you notice any damage to the Serb church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not -- I do not recall that it was damaged. It was not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any of the mosque in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw Mutnik mosque.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was its condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was ruined.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim homes at all that were left relatively intact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were only two or three along that road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were those two or three located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was in the downtown centre of Kozarac itself. I remember when I came back to the camp I was trying to explain to people there that it was an old house, a small old house that was intact. I was told it belonged to an elderly couple called Hasimic. I do not know those people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The other two Muslim homes that were relatively intact, where were they located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was located near the pastry shop that I mentioned before, and the third one was much further near the intersection of the road Banja Luka/Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These Serb houses that you mentioned, the four Serb houses, that were relatively undamaged, what was the condition of the houses on either side of these Serb houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were burnt.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall another occasion when you left the camp with a military escort and on that occasion saw the village of Kamicani burning?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown Prosecution Exhibit 79 again? If you could, please, look at that map for a moment to locate Kamicani? If that could be put on the overhead, please? Could you please show the court the area you are referring to as Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be an area here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on that a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is this area here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on that a little bit, please? I am looking at that and I do not see any village in that area that is called Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This whole area that went from Kozarac, when you leave Kozarac, and take the old road towards Banja Luka, about 500 metres after Kozarac, all of this area consisting of villages people would call "Kamicani" ---

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you show ---

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- in a wider sense of the word.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: -- us the area that people would refer to as "Kamicani"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicated). It would be from here, from this intersection that is located here, and this road that leads to Brdjani. Actually, all of this area and encompassing Softici, Alici, Rustici, Kesici, Donji Forici and all the area until Rustici would be called "Kamicani" in a wider sense of the word, including this area on the right side of the new Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. Then would you show for us again this area of Kamicani that you saw burning when you were taken from the camp by this military escort?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It could have been the area which is located here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the comment that the soldier made about this burning in Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The comment was, "When something like this, today Cigo are cleansing Kamicani and they will not be taken prisoners".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: "Today", I am sorry, would you repeat that? I do not understand the translation. The comment was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The comment was, "Today, Cigo's people or Cigo and his people are cleansing Kamicani. They will not be taken -- there will not be any prisoners".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On some of your other trips out from the camp at Trnopolje, did you go into the village of Trnopolje to look for supplies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who would escort you when you went into the village looking for supplies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we went into the gardens surrounding the camp Trnopolje, we would go out without an escort and maybe stay in the area of 200 and 300 metres around the camp that had the guards, but if I went any further than that, and that was mostly to help Serbian inhabitants, Serb inhabitants that were there or if any of the animals needed assistance, in that case I would have a military escort.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These times that you went into the village of Trnopolje, what did you see while you were in this village looking for supplies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would usually see that the houses that we passed by or that we entered, which also happened if we went looking for the medicine that perhaps was still in the houses, and that was at the times when we also had the escort, we could see that people left the houses in an incredible rush. The houses were totally, in a total chaos and mess. We could see that some furniture was missing, all the doors were open, all of the houses had the doors widely open.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of condition were the houses in? Were they damaged, were they not damaged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not damaged.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know the owners of any of those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those people that you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The owners that you knew, were any of those people in the camp at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were out in the village of Trnopolje, did you ever see looting being carried out at any of these houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was doing this looting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of things were they taking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taking everything, from furniture to little household items, food that they found in the houses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were out in the area of Trnopolje, the town of Trnopolje, did you ever see any abandoned Muslims' homes that were being occupied by other people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know the owners of those homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, where were the owners of those homes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those houses specifically, I knew a house that I knew that somebody had occupied, the owner of that house was in the camp in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to actually speak with the persons who were now inhabiting that home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you learn what their ethnic group was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were Serbs from Slavonska Pozega.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where that is, how far away that is from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not think it is more than 400 to 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is this a town or a neighbourhood, Slavonska Pozega?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I apologise. I did not understand the question. I thought you were asking me whether I knew where that house was located.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So the house was located 400 to 500 hundred metres from the camp and the persons living in the house, the town from which they had come, do you know how far away that was from Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not tell you exactly, but more than 100 kilometres probably.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did these individuals tell you why they were in this house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember they said that they also had to leave their houses, and that they had a much bigger and a much prettier house than the one that they got there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you would also leave the camp to go to provide veterinary services. When you left the camp for these purposes, what villages would you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually, those were Serb houses around Trnopolje. So I once went to Hrnici; a couple of times I went towards the village of Babici, Nisevici, or other villages that were on the road towards Prijedor, for example, Baltici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The condition of these Serb houses where you went, what was the condition of those houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were normal, not damaged.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated that at the Trnopolje camp while you were there, there were approximately 1500 to 2,000 men who were kept there permanently, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And that other people were brought in from surrounding villages which had been cleansed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people who were brought in from these surrounding villages, how long did they normally stay at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It varied, sometimes two, sometimes three or four but usually not longer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Three or four what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Days, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then after this three or four-day period, what was done with these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time they would be transported further.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How, what means of transport were used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first several groups, as we called them, convoys, were transported by the rail road, by the trains; whereas afterwards the convoys were transported on the road using the buses and the trucks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These transports by train, what types of railroad cars were used to transport these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly freight cars.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These buses and trucks that were used, were these civilian buses, civilian trucks or military buses and trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The people who were transported on these convoys, were they a mixed group or were they predominantly women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly women and children.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was done with the men who were brought to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The men, we either did not know what happened to them and where were they, or they were previously killed in villages or they were taken and remained in one of the camps.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So these groups who were coming into the camp from surrounding villages were predominantly women and children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The camp itself, I would like to ask you some questions about the conditions at the camp. First of all, what were the conditions like as far as hygiene is concerned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were impossible. We had no running water at all during the whole time we were there. The water was brought for the whole camp, it was brought from one well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The temperatures while you were in the camp that summer, was the weather very hot? Was it warm or was it cool that summer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that the first part of the summer was rainy and then after that it was very hot.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What about the toilet facilities for the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there was no water, insufficient water, the existing toilets in the school in Trnopolje could not be used and this is why in the meadow right next to the house the toilets were constructed temporary, temporary toilets.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were these open areas or were they enclosed areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were open, they were in the open, and the bricks that were found in the buildings, storage, the people made maybe a fence that were about, the fence that was about one metre tall, so that you could not exactly see into there and then around it they dug out the channels.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the shelter like at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry, I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Shelter at the camp, what were the lodging conditions, the shelter like at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean where the inmates were staying?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in the premises of the medical centre and the rest of the inmates were in the premises, on the premises, of the former elementary school in Trnopolje; and the people that were brought in were usually housed in the cinema building, and if all of them could not fit into those premises, then they would spend that night in the open.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These were the people who were brought in temporarily from the surrounding villages that were kept in the cinema?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not hear the first part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These were people who were brought in temporarily from the surrounding villages that were kept in the cinema?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The food at Trnopolje, how often did people have meals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no regular meals at Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times a day were people allowed to eat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People ate what they could find themselves, or what the villagers, while they still lived in their houses nearby brought them. As regards the camp itself, there were no organised meals, only from time to time, but it did not happen every day and there would be some military portions, some soup was provided for the inmates.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As a result of the conditions in the camp, did people develop any illnesses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of illnesses did they develop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the illnesses were usually the result of those appalling hygienic conditions. Lice was everywhere, then scab and diarrhoea was present to a large degree.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The translation says that they had "lice" and then "scab". I am sorry, I do not understand what you mean by "scab". Could you explain that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Scab is a skin disease -- do you want me to explain it?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are you talking about perhaps about scabies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am talking about scabies.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You had indicated that people were brought to Trnopolje from Keraterm and Omarska. Did you see these people when they were brought to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the general condition of these people brought from these two camps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Horrible, people were all only skin and bones. They looked like skeletons, one might say.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were any of the people brought from Keraterm and Omarska brought into the medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have document 5/20 brought up on to the computer screen, please?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is this an exhibit that is in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour. I would ask that this would be marked Prosecution Exhibit 206 for identification. (To the witness): Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the court wishes, we do have a photograph itself that we can actually offer as the exhibit. This would be marked as Prosecution Exhibit 206 for identification. Perhaps the witness could be shown that photograph? You indicated that you recognised this photograph. Who took this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Idriz Merdzanic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This individual that is shown on this photograph, was this one of the men who was brought to Trnopolje from either Keraterm or Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 206.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 206 will be admitted. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, at the time Dr. Idriz took this photograph, do you know what this gentleman's state of consciousness was? Was he conscious? Was he unconscious?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This photograph showing this man, was this indicative of many of the men who were brought to the camp from Keraterm and Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This man is what? Is he lying down here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is lying on the table on which we examine patients in the outpatient clinic itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: He is lying face down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, prone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If that photograph could be returned to the Registrar, please? During the time that you were in Trnopolje camp, to your knowledge, were people in the camp, detainees in the camp, beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: To your knowledge, how frequently did that occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Daily, one might say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: To your knowledge, where did these beatings occur, in what areas of the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In all of them, the school and from one could hear from people who were there, in the building of the outpatient clinic itself, that is, that office which used to be the laboratory once, then in a room which was next to the laboratory and which was the office of the Local Commune long ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Beatings which occurred in the laboratory, were you able to hear the sounds of those beatings as they were occurring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What did you hear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard the lashes or screams, sometimes curses.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you see detainees taken into that laboratory room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Then when they emerged would you see them with signs of beatings on their body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When they were taken into these laboratory rooms and then taken back out, who would take them in and who would take them back out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Military.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you recall on occasion where you were asked to come to the school and to examine a detainee at the school?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who was that detainee whom you were asked to examine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Nedzad Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you examined him in the school what was his condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was unconscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you see any signs on his body at that time, any signs of injuries, wounds, bruises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: This beating that he had received, was that the only beating that he had received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this was the second round of beating.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Where had the first round of beatings occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time he was beaten in the laboratory which was next to the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How soon after this first beating were you called to the school to see him as a result of his second beating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When you saw him in the school, did you determine that he needed care that you could not provide at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What were you concerned about that you felt he needed additional care?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, since he was unconscious, Dr. Idriz Merdzanic (who was also present) thought that his brain might have suffered some damage, and thought that he might die if he stayed with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you able to convince the personnel at Trnopolje to send him for care somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dr. Idriz Merdzanic turned to Dr. Ivic, who was also somewhere on the grounds of the camp there, and asked him to provide transportation for the patient which he promised to do when he went to Prijedor. But when we saw that Dr. Ivic had left for Prijedor and failed to take him along, we turned to guards and said that Dr. Ivic had said that the patient needed to be transported to Prijedor and they did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you subsequently learn where this man had been taken after his treatment in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we learned it. He was indeed taken to the hospital in Prijedor, and we then learned that from there he was taken to the camp at Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: After this gentleman had suffered the first round of beatings, did you or one of the medical personnel take photographs of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How soon after this first round of beatings were these photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A couple of hours later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: As a result of this first beating, what types of injuries did the man sustain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was so battered that we could not recognise him in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did he have any type of injuries or wounds on his body in addition to the bruises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was all covered in blood. One of his eyebrows was cut.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did he have anything that had been carved or marked on to his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In one part of his body, I cannot remember exactly where, one could see, and he spoke about that, that somebody had tried to carve a knife in him, but it was not a deep cut, a deep incision; it was more or less a superficial one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was the mark or symbol that had been cut superficially into his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If I could have document 5/18 called up on the screen, and if I could have this hard copy of this photograph marked as Prosecution Exhibit 207 for identification, please. If you could look at that photograph, please. Do you recognise the person in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nedzad Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is this one of the photographs that was taken of him by medical personnel shortly after his first series of beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 207.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 207 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I see a bandage over what appears to be the left side of his face. What is under that bandage? What type of injury is there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The skin and subcutaneous tissue were lacerated, had burst, next to the eyebrow and we sutured it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you look at his lower back, there is a very dark area there. What were the injuries in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were bruises, bloody, very big ones.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have 5/17 marked as Prosecution Exhibit 208 for identification, please. While we are looking at this -- if we could put the photo back on that was previously on -- while we are looking at this photograph, is there any place on this photograph that shows that cross that was carved superficially into his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you could please look at Prosecution Exhibit 208 for identification. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that also a photograph of Nedzad Jakupovic that was taken shortly after his first series of beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you look at that photograph, the areas of colour there indicate the bruising to his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Anywhere on this photograph can you see the cross that was carved into his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember where exactly, but I think it was somewhere in this area, either to the side or in the front, somewhere in the shoulder area. I know he asked us if it was visible and whether a scar would remain.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When he asked you that, was it visible to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one could see it, but I also remember that we told him that the wound was not deep, and that there would probably be no scar, at least not very visible.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If I could have this document marked as Prosecution Exhibit 209 for identification. This would be document 5/19. Is this Exhibit another photograph showing the area of bruises on Nedzad Jakupovic's body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This is another of the photographs you took very shortly after his first series of beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would tender Prosecution Exhibit 209 for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 209 will be admitted. Did you want to admit 208?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, I would also enter Prosecution Exhibit 208.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to 208?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: 208 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If those photographs could be returned to the Registrar, please. These beatings that occurred in Trnopolje camp, do you know any of the guards who administered these beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew them mostly by their nicknames.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the nicknames of some of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One was nicknamed Deba another one was called Darko. There was a Mile and there was one called Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where these guards were from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I know, for instance, that Darko was from Tukovi and Deba too. That is an area in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know the ethnic group of these individuals you have named?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall a man named Mujkanovic who was beaten at Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Over what period of time did the beatings of Mujkanovic last?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was beaten for a very long time, day and night.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see this man after this series of beatings were administered to him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him only as they were taking him from the clinic by the window, from the clinic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So he was being beaten in the laboratory area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During his beatings do you recall seeing Darko come outside and wipe his feet on the grass?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall Darko saying something at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was swearing and wiping off his boots. He said that he was bleeding.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: "He" being Darko was bleeding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he swore at the mother of that person in the laboratory and said,"Oh fuck his mother, how he's bleeding".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When Mujkanovic was taken out of the laboratory, do you know in what direction he was taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was taken in the direction of the railway station in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mujkanovic in the camp again after that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That same night that Mujkanovic was taken to the fish pond, do you recall seeing Darko come back to the medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that night Darko came to us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his condition when he came back to the medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was drunk.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall overhearing Darko talking to Sabiha Islamovic on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Drunk. I believe it was his birthday that day and he spoke about how it was his birthday that day, and how he was unhappy, how they were no people at all, how they were worthless. He also said that he was young, that he had done all sorts of things in his life, killed and set on fire and slit throats, and that the only thing he had never done before was rape.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As you were listening to these comments, did you hear Sabiha make any sort of comment back to this man Darko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was her reply?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She said, "Easy, sonny, you're young, there is still time to learn."

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did that reply confuse you at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever learn what she meant by that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you indicated that Darko had said that they were no people at all, they were worthless, to your understanding who was the "they" he was referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he was sort of saying, "We, the Serbs".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this may be an appropriate time to break.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of the gentleman who is in Exhibit 207, 208 and 209, Dr. Blazevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean Jakupovic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I do not recall the name.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He is a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The second gentleman you mentioned, Mujkanovic?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The one that was taken away, did not see him any more.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mujkanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: (2.30 p.m.) PRIVATE

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, you may continue.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, at the break we were talking about beatings that occurred at Trnopolje camp and those individuals who actually engaged in some of those beatings. I would like to ask you if you recall an incident in which a guard came to the medical clinic after participating in a beating to get his hand examined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did he want his hand examined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately before that he was in the lab, immediately before that he was in the lab, together with some other soldiers that were beating the detainees in the lab, and probably during that he injured his hand and he came in asking that we put a bandage.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he concerned that his hand was broken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall which guard this was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was a guard called Mladen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mladen's ethnic group was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were at Trnopolje, all of the individuals, all of the detainees, who were beaten at the camp, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of all of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The individuals who were involved in actually perpetrating these offences and beating these detainees, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Trnopolje camp, to your knowledge, was anyone killed at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the grounds of the camp one woman was wounded who immediately thereafter died, and one of the inmates who was beaten at the lab died in the lab itself.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know the name of that detainee who was beaten in the lab and then died as a result of the beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told that it was -- his name was Talic Teufik.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you actually see the body of Talic Teufik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only saw a body wrapped in a blanket.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did one of the medical personnel at the clinic tell you about this body and who it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who told you about this body and who it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was at the same time when Nedzad Jakupovic was beaten, and I think that I was told that by Nedzad Jakupovic himself, or by the people who knew that he was taken with Nedzad Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So Nedzad and Talic Teufik were taken together to be beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were brought into the lab at the same time and were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It was after that that Nedzad told you that the other man had died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were not told that by Nedzad; we were -- the soldiers brought Nedzad back to us, to the medical centre, so that we could help him if we could, and that in the evening hours or night hours, this was in the evening hours, and then in the morning they came to get Mujo, I think he was called Mujo, and told him to remove the corpse that was in the -- to remove the corpse that was in the lab.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was Mujo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mujo Zulic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he work there in the laboratory or in the medical clinic with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After he had removed the corpse then did he tell you who it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember that I have talked to him directly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. You mentioned a woman who was injured and then died. How did you know about that incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was brought into the medical centre as well after a shooting in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see of this shooting incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was an event in which a group of Serb soldiers that were standing at the entrance to the camp, right next to a truck, probably in negligence they shot out some bullets, as we heard later on, and during that incident a soldier was wounded. After that the guards or soldiers shot, fired very lowly, fired many times, throughout the camp in Trnopolje, and during that one of -- the woman was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was the woman who was brought to your medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: She died as a result of those injuries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know what her ethnic group was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Talic Teufik, did you know his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Trnopolje, did you learn of detainees who were taken out and made to dig graves and bury bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. While were you in Trnopolje camp did you learn of detainees who were taken out of the camp and forced to dig graves and bury bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were usually groups, people, who were inmates in Trnopolje, and the soldiers would from here to there take them out and ask them to do certain things.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then how would you learn about what they had done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After returning back they would tell us about where they were and what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually, they were burying the corpse, the corpses that were around the camp of Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they tell you what sites or what areas they were when they buried these corpses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they would tell us about it, where, how many, and if they recognised anyone they would tell us who it was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What areas did they tell you were the locations where they had buried bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Locations were different. For example, I remember that several times it was in the area that is located right next to the railway station in Trnopolje, in the area of Ribnjak fish pond. For example, it was also in the parts of the camp, parts outside of the camp towards Prijedor, simply all over in the area of -- perhaps one or two kilometres around the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The victims that the detainees identified, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these victims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in Trnopolje camp, did you learn of rapes that had occurred in the camp and in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Without mentioning the name of any victims, would you tell us, please, from whom would you learn about these rapes that occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would hear usually from the mothers of victims and the victims themselves.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: They would come to the medical clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, mothers would most often when very young girls, very young girls were involved, the mothers would come in concerned about the health of their daughters and concerned about the consequences and ask what could they do about it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say "concerned about their health", what types of problems would these young daughters have that the mothers were seeking advice about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mothers were normally worried that the girls would have -- would bleed profusely or, perhaps, become pregnant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident in which eight mothers brought their eight daughters to the clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they say had happened to these daughters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly how -- they simply did not talk openly about it. They would normally ask, what could we do, "Our daughters were taken out last night and they came back this morning and we are worried they may have become pregnant or start bleeding. Do you have something? Do you have any tranquilisers we could use?" and they would ask similar questions.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These daughters when they were brought into the clinic, what was their mental or emotional condition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually, they were crying and would not say anything.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These eight mothers and eight daughters who came to the clinic, did they indicate by whom they were taken out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they indicate where the sexual assaults had occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were taken out and taken towards Kozarac and it happened in a truck.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the age of these daughters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very young, 16, 17.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What medical care, if any, were they given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would give them, if we had any tranquilizers, we would give them, but in that specific case we turned to Dr. Dusko Ivic for help.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he, in fact, allow these young women to be taken to Prijedor and examined?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When they returned, did they tell you about their treatment in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember exactly. I mostly know that they were taken back -- they came back from Prijedor very shortly thereafter, and the same day they were sent with a convoy that was leaving Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you talked to Dr. Ivic about this incident, did you complain to him about the treatment of these eight young girls?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that Dr. Idriz did that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, did you learn of anyone being punished for these sexual assaults?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall after this soldiers coming to the camp in a tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These soldiers who came to the camp in a tank, do you recall why it was that they came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was an incident immediately after that. They asked, they requested that the person who turned them in and reported that they were raping, who reported that they did something similar, so they looked for that person and they said, "we would kill everyone".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this had occurred, do you recall a conversation with Dr. Ivic in which he cautioned you about causing problems?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told us that we saw into what trouble, what trouble we caused, as he said, what trouble we put them into, and he said it was best not to know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall him making any comment about rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said something like: "This is the war, this is what happens in a war and there is nothing we can do about it".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident involving a 13 year old girl being sexually assaulted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this was during the day close by to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who brought her to the clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mother.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they say had happened to her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They said that a guard took her out, took her into the house that was located across the street and raped her.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So she said that a guard from the camp did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not talk to her, Gutic Vasif talked to her and to her mother, and then told me this.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The eight young women that you talked about and this 13 year old girl, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of these young women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall an incident when a woman who was an acquaintance of yours came to you about a rape?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did she tell you had happened to her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: She just told me that one of the guards raped her near the camp in a house and that she wants to show me what guard it was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did she point out the guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this a guard that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one of the guards.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was the ethnic group of this guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you happen to recall at this time the name of that guard, if you ever knew it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What, if anything, did you, medical personnel, at the clinic advise young women and girls to do to try to escape being raped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would specifically say -- specifically it was that the women and children that were brought from the surrounding villages were always housed for one or two nights in the building of the cinema; and we noticed that the soldiers during the night come in and take out some of them and later we would learn that they were raped. Because of that, we were always trying to advise at least younger women and girls to spend that night in the school among the inmates because the soldiers very rarely went there during the night.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In addition to these rapes of young women who were in the camp itself, did you learn about rapes in the village of Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How would you learn about these rapes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be -- we would learn from the mothers who would come and tell us that they are worried because soldiers took away the daughter and did not bring her back the whole night. Usually, the mother would ask us -- because she would think that we knew more about it -- she would ask us who should she turn to for advice or ask us was there something we could do about it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These women who came to you in that fashion asking for information or advice, what was the ethnic group of these women?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have discussed several different incidents that occurred in Trnopolje camp while you were there. While you were in the camp, were you able to see every incident that occurred to detainees in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to see every Serb who came into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the camp would it have been possible for a Serb you knew to come to the camp several times and for you not to see that person?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would have been.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you ever told why you, yourself, were in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned earlier that there was discussion that people came to the camp or were brought to the camp to be protected from Muslim extremists, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they would always tell us that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there people you knew to be Muslim extremists in Kozarac before the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: We spoke earlier about the fact that some people in Kozarac did have weapons. Do you know how many weapons there were in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would go out into the town, would every person you saw, every Muslim you saw, in the town have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would every man in the town, every Muslim man, you saw have a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Could you say that most of the men you saw had a weapon? I am sorry, I did not hear the answer to that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But you did see some individuals who had weapons, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there some type of long-standing Territorial Defence plan that would place guards at important buildings in Kozarac in the event of war or emergency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a Territorial Defence plan -- I believe, at least, that there was one.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know about such a plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those plans existed during the existence of former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know about them? How did you know they were in existence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We would see them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you yourself have a duty assigned to you in case of emergency or war under this Territorial Defence plan?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: According to the Territorial Defence plan of the former Yugoslavia, or do you mean any other period?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Under the Territorial Defence plan that would have existed in the former Yugoslavia in the event of war or emergency, did you yourself have duties you were to carry out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have duties assigned to you under any other type of plan that may have been devised in the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, to your knowledge, were there guards at important buildings in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you yourself ever see such guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know if I could call this "guards", but in front of my house was one of the checkpoints where police and military were.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Between the time period of the Serb takeover of Prijedor and the attack on Kozarac, did you go out of your house after dark into the town of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you would be out at night during this time period, after the Serb takeover of Prijedor, before the attack on Kozarac, would you ever see men patrolling the town or guarding any buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were there, very likely, but I paid no attention.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to this conflict, were you or your husband a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you or your husband a member of any organised anti-Serb resistance group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the attack on Kozarac, did you or your husband become a member of any such group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At this time I would like to ask a few questions about a witness who has appeared here in this court and the witness has been referred to as "witness Q". When I ask these questions, please do not at any time indicate the name of witness Q. It is correct, is it not, that you have been informed of the name of witness Q?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It is true, is it not, that you did have a passing acquaintance with witness Q?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You would know witness Q, to see witness Q on the street perhaps somewhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to Sunday, 24th May when Kozarac was attacked. On that date, do you recall seeing witness Q at the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In fact, do you recall sharing a cigarette break with witness Q on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection at all of what witness Q was wearing at the time you saw witness Q?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have talked in your testimony here today about things that you saw Dule Tadic do, and you have talked about your knowledge of Dule Tadic and the fact that you had a passing recognition of each other or you of him. I would ask you at this time to look around the courtroom and if you see Dule Tadic in this courtroom, if you would, please, point to Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We object to this dock identification again, your Honour, for the same grounds as we did before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we believe that this is a recognition witness, that we have laid a sufficient foundation for this to be a recognition witness. Therefore, we do not believe the issues that would arise with an identification witness are present. We believe that this would be an appropriate question to ask and it would be appropriate for this witness to respond.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I will rule the same way I ruled before. Proper foundation has been made, just as it was made before. Therefore, I will overrule the objection. The witness has indicated that she knew Mr. Tadic before, and so I think a proper foundation has been made.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, would you look very carefully around the courtroom and see if you see Dule Tadic in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please point to Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the individual sitting between two policemen in the back row, in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic -----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The record will reflect that the witness has identified the accused.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you. (To the witness): Dr. Blazevic, you indicated that you left Trnopolje camp in August 1992. How were you able to leave the camp at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in mid August 1992 immediately after the International Red Cross entered Trnopolje when the camp Commander, Slobodan Kuruzovic, met me on the path in front of the camp itself where trucks and buses were already parked to take away the next convoy, and he told me, "You are going with this convoy."

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You were then taken with the convoy to Bosnian Muslim held territory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, close to that territory.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you transported from Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Trnopolje camp to a place on Vlasic Mountain, and people later told me it was called Smetovi and we were taken there by buses and then continued on foot.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic, when you went to Trnopolje on 26th May, did you go there because you truly chose to go there or because you had no real choice in the matter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not have any choice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In August, when you left Trnopolje, leaving behind your home and your local area, did you leave because you truly wished to leave or because conditions were such that you had no choice but to leave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because that was an order.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, is there cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic, I have some questions to ask you, first of all, about being interviewed: you have been interviewed by representatives of the Prosecution office during five days in November 1994?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I talked to them on another occasion with representatives of the official authorities of the country or the state that I live in at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You have signed a statement of that other interview?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was my first interview. I signed the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you get a copy of that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you clear up a matter I am quite unsure of, and that is when you started to practise in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I began to work in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In July 1983.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is it correct then that you moved to Kozarac in 1986, started to live there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You lived there up to May 1992, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Are you aware of any period of absence of Kozarac of Dusko Tadic in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Let us return to 1983. It was put to you by the Prosecution that you would have seen him in that year. Did you actually see him in that year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should like to explain something here. I knew names of people, of people in Kozarac, where they lived, their more or less family situation, and the like. However, I did not think every day about the accused, nor did I consider him such a close acquaintance to think about whether I had seen him yesterday or today. It was merely a person I met in passing. I knew where he lived, who was he was married to, and perhaps some other things if they would become interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If Dusko Tadic had been living abroad in these years or, at least, in that period of time, 1986 up to 1992, you would have known, would you not, or would you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be quite possible that I would not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Has Dusko Tadic ever visited your clinic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember that he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever visited his house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever been in his cafe?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You testified that on the third day of the attack, that is, Tuesday, May 26th, you travelled to Trnopolje to negotiate with the Serb authorities, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You also testified that the same day you returned to the motel where the medical centre was located in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not return to the motel, but to the medical centre in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Do you know at what time that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What does that mean, "before noon"? Can you give us a more specific time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know it could have been in the morning or noon, not later than that, but under the conditions, my temporal orientation was very bad because we had not slept for days -- for two nights already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. I am going to show you a map for identification. Could you tell us what the map shows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It should be a part of Kozarac, a central part of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I would like to tender this exhibit, your Honour. I think it will be D10.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: D12, the Registrar tells me. Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Defence Exhibit 12 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could it be put on the elmo, please, the whole of it, please? Thank you. (To the witness): Could you show on the map to us where you walked from the medical centre, as you have testified, to the intersection at the old Prijedor road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If I understand this map, the medical centre ought to be here and in that case we took this street here, and then this one which descends down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you also point out on this map where the pharmacy would be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If this is the road leading from the medical centre and this is Marsala Tita Street leading towards the intersection, then the pharmacy should be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Can you show on the map where the house of Dusko Tadic could be?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In that case Dusko Tadic's house should be roughly here on the other side of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point out to us where your clinic was, where you lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then it would be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Coming back to witness Q, and do keep in mind to refer to him as "witness Q", have you any idea where witness Q lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I may have a problem here doing this in open court, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I was wondering if the next question was, "Where, show me on the map".

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you handle the other cross-examination and then we could go into closed on that area, if you want?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Yes. If I may forget this, I will ask Mr. Kay to remind me.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. WLADIMIROFF (To the witness): Let us go back, first of all, to where you pointed out the medical centre on the map. Could you tell us were there other houses in the neighbourhood of the medical centre that were shelled? You can see in the map the houses, each house, located on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All along the road which we took from the medical centre towards the intersection of the old road and Marsala Tita Street in Kozarac, one could see the effect of shelling. There were either holes in the asphalt and houses were also damaged by those splinters which fell and some houses were hit directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So if you would be so kind as to point it out again on the map, starting at the medical centre, just how you walked and then tell us what you saw, all these houses while you walked up that street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We moved in this direction to the Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Stop here. So far, were all the houses you saw there shelled or hit by shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By and large, there were signs of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: If you continue on that road, Marsala Tita, you walk down to the intersection with the old Prijedor road, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If we continue down the Marsala Tita Street, then we reached the intersection with the old road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: While walking on the Marsala Tita Street, did you see houses that were shelled or at least hit by shells?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So am I right if I say that while walking from the medical centre up to the pastry shop most of the houses you saw in that area were shelled or hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, mostly all the houses in that area were damaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell the court what caused that damage? Was that because of the fightings in the street or was that the result of shelling from out of the hills?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: They were shot from outside the city on the city?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That happened during these three days or during the first two days? When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened from sometime on Sunday, around noon, when the shelling started in Kozarac until the moment when we left Kozarac.
