utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Let us move to the pastry shop. Could you point out on the map where that shop is? Could you point out the house which is drawn on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That ought to be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. You were standing there with a group, were you not? How many were in your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think 12 or 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How long had you been waiting there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, half an hour perhaps, or it could have been 10 minutes only. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: While you were standing there with your group, you were looking at what site? Were you looking at the pastry shop or were you looking at the Marsala Tita Street or were you looking over the triangle, square? In what direction did you look or did you look to each other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, each other mostly. We did look around but such fear reigned and I could not really define it. At any rate, we were standing and talking.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you able to move within your group or did you just stand as you stood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you able to move within your group or were you just staying there not moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not move.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How many people did you see on the triangle, square?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were there lots of people or just some?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember there were two groups of soldiers, perhaps four or five persons each. I remember that two soldiers were in front of a house which was there by the road. There were also some soldiers by the school, but whether there were very many or just a few, I could not tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were there just soldiers in these two groups standing in two groups or were they moving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The two groups were standing and some very few, some of them moved about. Those two in front of that house moved about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you see anyone crossing who belonged to these groups of soldiers, crossing the street or crossing the square?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you see people crossing on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember. I do not think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You testified that at a certain moment you looked up because someone said, "There is Dule". Saying that you "looked up", would that indicate that you were looking to the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Highly likely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, apparently, by this reference to "There is Dule", you were triggered to look around; that was the only reason why you looked around, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: "Dule" is a Serb name, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a nickname.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How many people do you know by the nickname "Dule" in those days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A few.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you point us out on the map where you saw this person that was crossing that was referred to as "Dule"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The map, it would be exactly here where these two small streets join, right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You testified that you saw him "just a few seconds", did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you describe to us his appearance, how he looked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was dressed in a uniform. In one hand he had a weapon and the other one was high up in the air, so it seemed as if he was talking to someone or trying to draw someone's attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you describe his face?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You further testified that you saw Dusko Tadic two days before the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day or two before the attack, I know that he was still in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you did not actually see him two days before the attack or did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two days, I cannot tell you for a fact that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So when was the last time you saw him before the attack?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would try to explain again that the person that I see during the day, I do not take that as a special event, I do not consider that a special event, because generally this does not signify anything to me. I have said before that I have known the accused one on a passing by basis. So the person that I probably met daily, I would remember that person only if there was something special about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But you have no special recollection of meeting Dusko Tadic before the attack on Kozarac, have you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw him in the days immediately prior to the attack on Kozarac, immediately before the attack on Kozarac, but what was the day when I saw him last time, I truly cannot tell you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Seeing him before the attack then, unspecified, just seeing him; have you seen Dusko Tadic ever before in a uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you ever seen him before with a gun, with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is possible that he had one, but I really did not notice that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You also testified that you recall a meeting or, at least, having or shared a cigarette break with witness Q in the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So I take it you smoked a cigarette together, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. So how long would that take, to smoke a cigarette?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever it takes, two or three minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. In order to testify you cannot recall what witness Q was wearing at that time, can you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you smoked during two or three minutes a cigarette with him, but you do not know what he was wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I normally do not notice that unless there was something peculiar, special, about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Let us return back to this incident on the triangle square. You were brought there with the group coming from the medical centre taken by soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: While you were waiting there, the soldiers came again and they told Nihad Bahonjic to go with them. I suppose you were all standing there not moving, being afraid, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You did look to the ground when someone said to you, "That's Dule"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, nobody told me "This is Dule", we just heard a whisper saying, "There goes Dule", which for us meant that somebody that we knew was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So when someone whispers "There's Dule", you looked up, saw in a very split second or a few seconds a person in a uniform, you have no recollection of his face, you cannot tell us, and you tell us that you saw Dusko Tadic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic, I suggest you were mistaken by thinking that you saw Dusko Tadic at that intersection, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not believe that I was mistaken, because at that moment when I looked around me, looking for a familiar face, I was not looking to see the accused, but simply the person that was crossing the street was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before you entered in this courtroom yesterday, did you have a witness document giving you a layout of the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Before you entered this courtroom yesterday have you been shown the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The courtroom, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Has it not been told to you where the parties were sitting, where the Judges were sitting, where the accused is sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told where the Judges sit, where the Defence sits, where is the Prosecution and, as far as the accused is concerned, I was told that he, the accused, may sit anywhere in the courtroom or not sit there at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you not suppose that the accused would sit on the side of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have no need to suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You were shown, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know him and it does not matter to me where he sits. I can recognise him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: He is to sit between two policemen, as you testified?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I think we are only left with this issue of the house of witness Q, as far as I am concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I think, your Honour, after conferring with Mr. Kay, we feel it might not be necessary, seeing the answers.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. Have you finished your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have finished the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Do you have any redirect, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Very quickly, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic, you have indicated that the shelling of Kozarac began on 24th May and continued into 26th May. Were there periods when the shelling of Kozarac was very heavy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there other periods when the shelling of Kozarac became very sporadic and very light?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the period of time during which the shelling of Kozarac was the heaviest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The most intensive shelling was during the night, on Sunday the whole day, on the night between -- in the night between Sunday and Monday, and on Monday until approximately the afternoon hours, or the evening hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then after that the shelling became much lighter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On Tuesday was the shelling very sporadic on that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At what time of the day did you arrive in Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the sunset.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you have any idea how long it took you to travel from Kozarac to Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not remember because at first we waited in Kozarac at the intersection, and then we were taken to Zikina tavern where we also waited, and then we were taken -- we were taken on an alternate road to Trnpolje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Regarding witness Q, you have indicated that you saw witness Q on Sunday, 24th; that you recalled sharing a cigarette break with witness Q on that date. Do you recall on that date witness Q assisting with preparations at the medical centre?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a group of young men from the neighbouring area that were during those several days they were with us at the medical clinic trying to help us with what we were doing there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is it your recollection that witness Q was among that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were at the intersection on 26th May, was there anyone obstructing your view, anyone or anything obstructing your view, when you looked and saw Dule?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you looked and saw Dule, the Dule whom you saw, was that the Dule Tadic that you knew had a cafe and house on Marsala Tita Street in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Just one, your Honour. I will show the witness a paper on which I have written the real name.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Sorry, I do apologise. I will show the witness, your Honour, a paper on which I have written down the real name of witness

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to ask her whether this is the name she had in mind when we are talking about witness Q. I will show it to the Prosecution, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Show it to the Prosecutor, fine. Will the usher please pick that up and show it to the Prosecutor and then we will put it before Dr. Blazevic? Please put it flat down on the table and flat on the table. Put it flat on the table.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is the name you were referring to when talking about "witness Q"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I just have one question or perhaps two.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Dr. Blazevic, you have testified about the hospital in Kozarac and I have heard it referred to as a hospital, a medical centre and a clinic. Would you tell me, what is it? Was it the only hospital in town or in Kozarac, or tell me what it was, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Officially, it was called Health Centre in Kozarac, and it was a building in which one could have a routine medical examination, where one could have routine lab tests done, blood tests, and similar, that also had some dental offices and that would be all.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Did persons remain there overnight for treatment or for extended periods?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: There were no hospital beds there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were no beds.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Was there a hospital somewhere else in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: And no other medical clinic in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- I apologise, it is possible that, just as in Trnopolje, there were premises within the Local Commune premises, there were offices where doctors would see patients.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: But this was the only medical facility, I suppose, then in Kozarac, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You have testified that you came back to Kozarac on two occasions after you were taken to Trnopolje camp. My notes, at least, indicate that the first time was two or three days after you arrived at the camp, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Then you came back a second time on a bicycle escorted by soldiers, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was on the bicycle alone on the area from Trnopolje to Suhi Brod because at that time that area was still inhabited by people that lived here before the war, and it was -- the freedom was relatively -- the movement was relatively unimpeded there, and from Suhi Brod I had a military escort.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: You were taken to Trnopolje on what date? Was it the 27th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was on 26th.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: So you would have come back the first time then around, whenever, 29th or so of May, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, possibly.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: OK. When did you come back a second time? That is what I really wanted to ask you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly but it must have been about 20 or so days after that, maybe even more than 20 days.

utterances.speaker: THE COURT
utterances.text: Were there any Muslims in town, in Kozarac, the first time that you came back?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, do you have additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We will stand in recess then for 20 minutes now and then you may call your next witness when we return, Miss Hollis or Mr. Niemann. Very good.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I call Nasiha Klipic. NASIHA KLIPIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you please take that oath?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated. You may proceed, Mr. Niemann.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Mrs. Klipic, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how far is that from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I should say three to 3.5 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you attend primary school in Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you then attended a dress making course in Prijedor where you graduated in 1979?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you then work in your family's private business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we did not have a private shop. We had our trucks, our tractors, horses, and we used to transport building materials, timber, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was that private business or where was that business, your family business?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At home.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Was that in Kamicani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, in Kamicani.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you put your headpiece on the top of your head it will stay in place, I think, for you. You will not have to hold it. Did you stay there until you were married?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, until '87.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you marry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sahinuk Klipic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did your husband do, what was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What sort of work in the police did he do? What was the area of police work that he did?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband completed the traffic police school and he worked in Prijedor police, depended on what there was to do, like any other policeman around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. For how long did he work in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband worked until 29th April '92, between 29th and 30th, until the power was taken over in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened to him when the power was taken over in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My husband worked until 11 o'clock. He came to the Prijedor railway station and from there the last bus was leaving at half past 11, but the bus had not gone and he went into a tavern, into a place near the railway station, and he asked some colleagues to take him home; they were Rade Strika and Preradovic, and they said they had no time to drive him home, and then he returned, went out on the road to Kozarac and hitch-hiked some transport, and then he arrived home at about 2 or 3 o'clock. He said: "Well, I survived this, I do not think I will be able to survive again another night like this".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he then commence work as a policeman in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Since Muslims and Croats could not return to Prijedor to work as policemen, then they all started working at the nearest place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In his case that was the Kozarac police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: As a consequence of your husband's occupation, did you come to know a number of police officers in the Prijedor region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you also familiar with the some of the police that worked in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In fact, although your husband worked in Prijedor, you lived in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If we could have photograph 6/6 brought up on the screen, please, and would you look at this photograph that I now show you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the -----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry, but that should have been marked by the Registrar first. Could it be marked as the next number in line, 210? Just looking at the photograph that you have in front of you which is also displayed on the screen, can you tell me what the photograph is or what it shows in part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We see crossroads here. There was a checkpoint where there were policemen, Serb policemen. Until Sunday 24th, until the attack at around 11 o'clock, that is where they were; and we lived in this house here, and this big building is the printers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. I tender that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 210 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just looking at the photograph as it appears on the screen, is your house the house that you can see in the far right of the photograph, near the pole?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Now it is on the far right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just tell us again where is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Next to what is -- next to the Banja Luka/Prijedor highway, near the petrol pump.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender that, your Honours. Perhaps that might be handed back to the Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you in Prijedor just prior to the commencement of the attack on that town in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Just prior to the attack, can you tell us where were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Prior to the attack on Kozarac, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 20th April '92, we went to the employment office since we were out of work so I had to report every two months to the employment bureau, so that was the day when I went there, on 28th April '92.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: But the attack on Kozarac is what I am talking about, not Prijedor. Can you recall where were you when Kozarac itself was attacked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was visiting a colleague of mine, Marsala Tita Street, they were Tinka and Fadil, Tinka and Fadil, that is where they lived. They were our closest friends from Kuljani; and I was there, Thursday and Friday, Saturday, until the attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember what dates these were in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 21st, 22nd, 23rd, 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On 24th, were you with your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: About what time was the town of Kozarac attacked in the day, about what time in the day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it was, I am not sure, but perhaps 1.00 or 2 o'clock p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you with your husband at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did your husband stay with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, my husband left. When the siren sounded my husband went to the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Was your husband on duty that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do when your husband left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When my husband left, my colleague and I took my two children and her child and her husband and we went to a shelter to Nafik Hamic. That was the cellar of the house. That is where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was this cellar in this house that you went to? Was it in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was it just somebody's, one of your neighbours' cellars, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then once you went into the cellar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, then a major fire began. The oddest thing in the world, the hardest moment in one's life, shells were falling. It was very hard on us. We were sitting there screaming, crying.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At this stage you still had your children with you, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately, how many people were with you in the cellar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about 20, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown Exhibit 196? If that could be placed on the -- (To the witness): First of all, do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is it? What do you recognise it as?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the Prijedor/Banja Luka road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is it a plan, as you understand it, of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you put that on the screen and could you take up the pointer, please, and looking at it would you point to, firstly, approximately where your house was in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the intersection Prijedor/Banja Luka, Prijedor. I think it is somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Can you tell me where you went to where the cellar was, the house that had the cellar that you went into and took protection, approximately where was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think up the Marsala Tita Street or high street. Here is the play field and then towards the hospital. I think this is where one turns to the hospital. The house was somewhere here. It was the third building from the main street towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So down the side street? Was it down the side? Was it in the side street off Marsala Tita Street?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was right next to -- if this is the high street and you turn here, I cannot exactly remember, then I think you take this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I do not know whether it is terribly important, but I am somewhat confused as to where the witness's house was and the house that she went to where the cellar was, because when she moves the pointer sometimes she does not stop when she means to stop. So just take your time and tell us. It is important for us to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you pick up the pointer, first of all, I would like you to go back to where your house was on that plan and just leave it still at that spot.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My house was, if this is -- I really have a problem. If this is the high street and you turn up there, so my house could have been here at this intersection; if I go from Prijedor to Banja Luka, it was on the right-hand side, and if I go from Banja Luka to Prijedor, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I want you to assume -- if you are a bit confused just say so because we can take it more slowly -- that going to the left is going towards Prijedor and going to the right on that road is going towards Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am lost. I simply am lost. I know it is here but on which side it is, I do not know. As a matter of fact, it is on that picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. It is in that general area, that is where your home is, if you can say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: All right. Can you go back and tell me where it was that you went to when the attack started and you went into the cellar? Can you possibly point that out on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I go here, this is the school, and I think I turn here, this is -- and we move towards the hospital. Am I following the right direction? Yes, I go towards the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The little square with the "H" in it, assume that for a moment is the hospital, does that help you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I think I was here, yes, right in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. Might that exhibit be returned, your Honours? How long did you stay in that basement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there until Monday morning, until 8 o'clock. It was the 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened on Monday morning, 25th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The military had already entered Susa and Kozarac down there to the asphalt, and some people ran up to us and told us to take our children and run towards the woods. But as the shelling was going on, we did not dare come out of the shelter, it was dangerous; and we, nevertheless, decided it was better to be killed by a shell than be slaughtered, or whatever they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you give your evidence, can you give it very slowly because it has to be translated and otherwise people cannot translate it if you talk too fast. So when you answer my questions, could you do it as slowly as you possible can?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So you decided with these other group of people that you would go into the woods. Where did you go? In which direction did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went towards Brdjani, towards Kozara, it is called Brdjani and then Krtavina and then there was a youth hostel up there that we went -- well, all in all, we went to the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "we", how many people approximately were in your group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we, I was driven by a neighbour who had a green Mercedes and my children and my colleague's child and his mother and they came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: By this stage had you seen your husband?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look, please, at the photograph that I now show you and might photograph Z5/21 be brought up on the computer screen, please. Just before you do that, could you mark that copy, have the Registrar mark that copy, please? Looking at that photograph, what is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is my husband and his two brothers and sister-in-law and his colleague, a Serb policeman. My brother-in-law was roofing -- was putting the roof on his house so they had a party. They were celebrating it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The original photograph that you have there in front of you that is being shown to you is the only copy that survived the attack in Kozarac, is that right? It is the only copy you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do have some more but this one I was given by my sister-in-law. I have none of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Your Honours, I tender the copy rather than the original, although the original is available for inspection and we can make available copies from the computer which produces quite reasonable reproductions of that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: If the witness wishes to retain the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Is there any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK. Exhibit 211 then will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now perhaps those photographs could be returned? (To the witness): Once you went away in the green Mercedes Benz, where did you finally arrive? Where did you finally come to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We arrived at a house, it is called mountaineers' home, and we got off there and he returned to fetch other people, those who had stayed behind in the shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there a number of people gathered at this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do when you got to this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We did not know where to go. In the forest, shells were falling on the forest, so we went to some bushes and we hid there, but they could see us there so that is where the attack was the most ferocious.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did you stay at this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there until the evening when it became dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The evening of 25th or 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 25th.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we left to Adil, Adil and Nasiha Jakupovic had their summer cottage there. There we spent the night.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: These were friends of yours, were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened after that, after that night? Did you continue to stay up in the mountain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we stayed there until Tuesday afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say Tuesday afternoon, that is 26th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could not stay up there any longer because of the shelling, because of the fire and ---

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- and then we decided, since we were a large group, I do not know how many, to go towards Vidovici. There was a small Serb village, I do not know how many houses, but it was a very small one and it was not shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to give any estimate of the number of people that were moving down towards Vidovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think we were very many, I cannot say 2,000 or 3,000, but it was a long column.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In this group were there women and children and men?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were these people, people from the surrounding area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got to the village of Vidovici -- just before I ask you that, how far is Vidovici from Kozarac centre, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Five kilometres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you got to Vidovici, what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We arrived there, to Milan Vidovic's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you take shelter there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we spent the night there and we were there until Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This is Wednesday, 27th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened on that day, Wednesday 27th? What did you do that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On Wednesday, 27th, we were with Vidovici's, the army had already arrived at the Brdjani, to the mosque. They were setting everything on fire. Houses were burning and then we realised there was nothing else to do but to surrender, to go down and we decided to go towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have your children with you at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your husband with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How did you travel down towards Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I and my children were on a tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say you were on a tractor, were you sitting on the tractor itself or a trailer that was being towed by the tractor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On a trailer, we were on a trailer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were some people walking and some on a tractor and some going by other forms of transport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some were riding in a car, some by tractors and some walked.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know the accused Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long have you known him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost all my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you recall any circumstances in particular that you can recall meeting the accused Dule Tadic, any particular circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew Dule. Sometimes he would say "Hi", sometimes we would not, but I think that in 198 -- I think in 1985 or 6 in a tavern, in "Neima".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did something happen there that you can especially recollect when you think of Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was funny and weird.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened, tell us, in this cafe in 1986?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was with my brother and other friends there. I was in Bihac at a wedding, and then we went back to Neima to have a drink.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "Neima", is that the name of the cafe, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was called "Neira".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was that cafe, what town was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "Neira" was, I think, eight or nine houses down from the house of Dule in the Marsala Tita Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In Kozarac, was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You went into this cafe after going to a wedding that you had attended in Bihac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we went and wanted to sit at a table. Dule Tadic and his company, I do not remember who was there, but I think one of his brothers was there. I wanted to sit down and the chair was behind me and Dule pulled the chair away to try to make a joke.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I tried to sit down and I missed the chair and I fell down.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. During your life, how often would you have seen the accused Dule Tadic, on an average?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very frequently, because I was frequently visiting taverns and cafes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where Dule Tadic lived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did he live?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dule Tadic lived in Kozarac. In Marsala Tita Street, there was a restaurant and the house of Banda and he was next to Banda's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Banda was his neighbour, was he, his immediate neighbour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, first neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: If you stood in Dule Tadic's house and faced Marsala Tita Street, would Banda have been on the left or on the right-hand side of Dule Tadic's house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It would be to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know who the neighbour was of Dule Tadic on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was Suljo Mujagic and Adil Jakupovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Looking directly across, if you stood in front of Dule Tadic's house and looked directly across Marsala Tita Street, what would you see on the other side of the road?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the other side of the road there was a building, people lived there. Below that building was another building which had a barber shop, pharmacy and a textile store.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you look at the photograph that I now hand to you and perhaps it might be marked 212? Perhaps it might be brought up on the screen? It is 49/15. Would you just look at the photograph that has been handed to you there, and can you tell me, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is it a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This here was a barber shop -----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, no. I am sorry. We cannot point to it on the screen because it does not come through, we cannot see what you are pointing at. So if you can just tell me what it is in your own words, if you would not mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a building, upstairs is where the people lived, and on the lower level -----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that a photograph of the building that you just described a moment ago as being opposite Dule Tadic's place, across the road from Dule Tadic's place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is a little below there and the house that I spoke before was a little bit above this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Tell me what that is a photograph of? Is that near Dule Tadic's house, that photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is across from the restaurant. It is very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see, thank you. Is that the house that you were just describing a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. I tender that, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No objection, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Exhibit 212 will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Might that photograph be put on the elmo for me, please? Perhaps it could be made larger. (To the witness): With the pointer would you point, please, to the part of that building which is closest to Dule Tadic's house if you were looking across the road? You cannot point to the computer screen, I am afraid; you will have to point to the elmo, this screen here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am sorry. This.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That there? What is that? Is that a shop premises immediately above your pointer that you have just pointed to, is that a shop?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, this is a barber's shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, and is there a shop immediately beside that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is a pharmacy, and this is a textile shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Above those shops do people live, do they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Perhaps those photographs could be returned? Before the war in 1992, did you know what Dule Tadic did for an occupation, for a living?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Dule as a coach, as a Karate coach.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What about the premises where he lived, was there any business attached to that premises?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In the last years he opened a cafe and had a private cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what the name of that cafe was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I forgot. It was not interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know what his father's name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What is his father's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think Ostoja.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know his wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where she worked?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where did she work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His wife, Mira, worked at the medical centre, in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he had any family, any children?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Dule Tadic had two daughters.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately what age were they, roughly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember that one was older, and the younger one was eight or nine, like my son.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: That is eight or nine now, is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Younger, I think so, around that age and the older one, 12 or 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know any of his friends or any of the people he used to associate with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to name any of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Dule Tadic was the most frequent friend of Emir Karabasic, Vaso Crnogorac, Fadil Hrustic, Adil Jakupovic, and almost everyone in Kozarac. He was on good terms with almost everyone, but those were the people that I saw him most frequently with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were those people that you mentioned Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know whether Dule Tadic had any brothers or sisters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he had two or three brothers. I mostly know him and his brothers, not .....

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to speak to Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this only once or did it occasionally happen during the time that you were living in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, many times. In passing by, we would say "Hello" to each other. My brother, Envir, gave some lumber to Dule Tadic for his cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your brother's name, Envir was his first name, what was his second name, his surname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Envir Alic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How old was your brother, Envir Alic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother Envir was born in '49.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What did he do in Kozarac? What was his occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My brother, Envir, did not work in Kozarac. He worked in Sisak.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a truck driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you seen your brother since the war, since 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know where your brother was taken shortly after the outbreak of the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was he taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You have never seen him since?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you also have another brother, Ekrem?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Would you like to have a drink of water?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We can take a few moments, Miss Klipic -- am I pronouncing that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I am fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your other brother, Ekrem, how old would he have been?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was born in 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Have you seen him since the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What of your husband, after that day he left in May 1992? Have you seen your husband since that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: We got to the point in your evidence where you had started to come down in a trailer behind a tractor. Can you tell us what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at that time the convoys started and we were going down from Brdjani. The army was there. Everything was burning, houses, mosques, everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far would Brdjani be approximately from the centre of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about two-and-a-half or three kilometres. Brdjani are quite large.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. As you came down, tell us what you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I came down, we came to the intersection Kozarac, in Kozarac, and we started towards Prijedor -----

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This was Wednesday, 27th May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. Approximately what time of the day was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think around 2 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I know it is very hard for you to estimate these things, but approximately how many people were coming down in that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can say that the column was from the intersection in Kozarac up to the pastry shop, perhaps one or two kilometres long.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: OK. Did you see some military tanks and things of that nature in the area or the vicinity as you came down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What else did you see as you came down in that column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We saw anything, everything, terrible things; dead people, cows; houses burning; we saw many soldiers; policemen; tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The policemen that you saw, were you able to determine from looking at them whether they were people you knew as Serb policemen or were they some Serb and some Muslim policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All Serbs; there were no Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we started towards Kozarusa. We walked towards Kozarusa and I mostly paid attention to policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Why were you paying attention to policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because up until that day those were colleagues of my husband and I knew them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you also looking for your husband as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I asked them if they knew something about my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who did you ask?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we -- when I went towards Prijedor when I was on the tractor, there was a Golf car, a police Golf car, driving towards Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "a Golf", do you mean a Volkswagen Golf car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we used to call that police Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. What colour was this car, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a police colour, blue and white.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: This was a car that you had from time to time become familiar with because of your husband's duties as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see who was driving the police car that came towards you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now as this police car came towards you, you were still in the trailer, were you, behind the tractor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was the police car coming up the same direction as you were going or was it coming from the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have an opportunity to look at who was driving the police car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And who was driving it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The driver was Brane Bolta.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You had known him obviously prior to this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he worked for 10 years I think in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: He worked as a policeman?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was his nationality or ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there anyone else in that car that you recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Who was ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brane Bolta and next to him was Dule Tadic and then Goran Borovnica, and then I could not see if somebody was sitting next to Goran Borovnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: So immediately beside the driver in the passenger seat is that where you say you saw Dule Tadic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was Goran Borovnica sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Goran Borovnica was sitting behind Bolta.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For how long were you able to look at this police car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was just perhaps a minute or two. We were standing and they were slowly driving because they could not drive fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did that police car stop at any stage or did it just slowly drive past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They slowly past us. I was yelling "Bolta, Bolta", of course I was only interested in the policemen so could I ask them about my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did Bolta appear to respond at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Approximately how close did you get at any one stage to that police vehicle or how close did the vehicle get to where you were sitting at its closest point, approximately?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Less than a metre, perhaps just half a metre because there was just a white dividing line between us, between the tractor and the Golf car; perhaps half a metre or 80 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were the windows of the car opened or closed, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember; perhaps open a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you recognise Dule Tadic when you first saw him or at some later stage as the vehicle approached where you were sitting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I recognised him then and afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know Goran Borovnica before this day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Goran Borovnica was a waiter in the Red Rose tavern.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now at the time you saw this police vehicle in which you saw Dule Tadic, what were the weather conditions like? Was it fine or overcast, can you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was very warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And the sun was shining?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was your view in any way obstructed at any time as this vehicle came up and drove past you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Well, did anything at any point as this vehicle was coming up to where you were sitting and drive past, at any point did anything get in your road or anything to stop you from seeing the vehicle, any obstruction in your way during that period as it past?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was happy to see a police car and learn the truth about my husband.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I think you said a moment ago that you addressed Bolta but he ignored you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Had you seen Dule Tadic and Borovnica together on any previous occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where had you seen them together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the taverns in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see them only occasionally or did you see them often or perhaps you cannot say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you remember seeing how Dule Tadic was dressed, appeared to be dressed when he was sitting in that car?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What do you understand by a "camouflage" uniform? What sort of -- can you describe that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is the multi-coloured uniform. It is an unusual uniform because until the war we did not have such a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Now after that vehicle passed, what did you then do?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went for a long time, perhaps an hour, until Kozarusa and Zikina tavern.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Kozarusa, is that on the road that goes between Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far would Kozarusa be, approximately again, from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about five kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: In this column that was going along the road that you were in at this time, were some people walking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were some people, as you were, travelling on a motorized vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again, were there women and children in the group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: And men as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was there anyone guarding this column or walking with this column not part of it at the same time as you were going along?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean, that Serbs guarded us?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were singling people out and killing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see this happen yourself or was this something someone told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we saw when they were singling the people out, but they were taking them into the houses or above the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "Serbs", were they army, were they police or were they a mixture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a huge mix.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you know what people in the, the uniform of a JNA officer looked like, a JNA soldier looked like? Are you familiar with that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see people who were dressed in a JNA uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You were obviously familiar with the uniform that the police officers or police wore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you see people dressed in those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Tell us again, how long did it take you to get from, say, Kozarac to where you set off up to Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In those moments I do not know how many hours, but we travelled from afternoon until evening. I think perhaps an hour and a half it took us to get to Kozarusa.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at Kozarusa, what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The saddest, the worst things happened. They separated men from 15 to 65 years of age from their wives and mothers, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "they" you are referring to the Serbs, are you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us where it was in Kozarusa that this was happening?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Kozarusa there was a bus station and I was standing precisely at the bus station.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was this on the main road between Kozarac and Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: At Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from the bus station, were there any other buildings that you remember around the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a Zikina tavern and a large, well, not large but a big parking lot by the road, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there any vehicles there, any vehicles that had been parked there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were very many vehicles. I think there was a tank, an amoured vehicle, I cannot remember exactly, right by Zikina tavern.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Apart from the amoured vehicle, were there buses and any other forms of vehicles there that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The Serbs that were doing this sorting out, did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Are you able to name any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me try to remember, Mile Preradovic, Rade Strika, Ranko Durdevic, Dule Tadic, Goran Borovnica, Tomo Stojakovic, Duro, I cannot remember his surname, another traffic policeman. I mean there were almost all policemen those whom I knew best.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Could you see what these particular people that you named were doing at the time when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were separating men in three groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What were the three groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they were for Omarska, others for Trnopolje and some for Keraterm.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How did you know that this was the classification of each of the groups, Trnopolje, Keraterm and Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were not sure where they were going, but then I learned that they were taken in that direction later.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Again when you saw Dule Tadic, how far away from him were you when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was about three or four metres, that was very near across the asphalt and on that lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you first saw him were you standing, were you sitting? Can you tell us where you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were you sitting in that trailer that you mentioned earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you still have your children with you at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were the conditions, the lighting and so forth, still good at this time so you could have a clear view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Between where you were sitting and where you saw Dule Tadic, were there any obstructions or anything that interfered with your view of him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: For approximately how long were you able to look at him while he was in that place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We spent a lot of time there. For how long did we watch them? Well, they moved around, "You, hey, you, don't go here, come on there". I do not know the least. I mean I did not pay much attention to him. I watched others more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I see. Did you hear Dule Tadic say anything at that stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he loudly asked Milos: "Where do I take these? Where do we take these", and the other one, at any rate, they were both closely co-operating there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you say "Milos" who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milos the policeman, Milos Preradovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Where was he from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was from, I would not know, Kernica or from where, but he had spent in Kozarac a long time as a policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: You said Goran Borovnica was there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What was he doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same as all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you heard Dule Tadic talking there, did you recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean "recognise"? I saw him shouting "Hey, you".

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you tell us how he was dressed on this occasion when you saw him at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He had a camouflage uniform,. He was bare headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Was he carrying any arms that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, an automatic rifle and a pistol with a belt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he have any other weapons on his person that you could see?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not see it. This I saw, I know these best because my husband had an automatic rifle and a pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did he speak to you at any stage while you were sitting there in that trailer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What happened then to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brane Bolta approached and asked me if I had anyone in Prijedor to go to. I said I did not and I wanted to go where my people went.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you think Brane Bolta was prepared to help you if he could?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, perhaps just to show that he was a man of character.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes. So, what happened to you when you said you had no one in Prijedor that you could go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then Brane Bolta was at the end of the column and Tomislav Stojakovic and there was also a police car, I do not know which one, they took us to the camp in Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How far is Trnopolje approximately again from Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think about six kilometres from Kozarac to, it was also called Kozarac but it is Trnopolje in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How did you get from Kozarusa down to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were following a road that I had never taken before in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I mean did you walk or did you go by vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The tractor again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The other people that were in the group that went down to Trnopolje, were they taken in any form of motorized transport or did some of them walk as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were no more people; there were only women and children there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know, again it is difficult for to you estimate, but approximately how many women and children were in that group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Very many, awfully many. I could feel from the way they cried I could feel how many there were, because it was sadness, it was terribly sad to look at because men were taken away and you were going you did not know where.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Were there any men in the group at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They only let those very advanced in age or somebody very young to drive the tractor or horses or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get from Kozarusa down to Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were going towards Donji Garevci, to Orlovci, Donji Garevci, and then I do not know, an hour perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Can you remember what time it was approximately when you arrived at Trnopolje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know soon after the darkness came.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived there what happened then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stayed there in the camp, that is in this place with wire and there were very many, many people there already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Had you been to this place before, prior to the war, prior to 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every May 2nd we had a big popular outing there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The place where the camp was, what was it used for before it was used as a camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was a school, a shop, and there was a warehouse, a hardware store, there was a centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you arrived at this place, did there appear to be people guarding the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether these people were Serbs or were they Muslims or are you able to tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Muslims were inside the camp and the Serbs were guarding the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Do you know whether they were members of the police or the army or both?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: When you first arrived there where did you stay the first night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A relative came to me and took me to the third house from, as one goes from the camp towards Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Did you have your children with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: How old were your children at this stage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two and a half and four and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes. On Tuesday we will be having an initial appearance in another matter. I thought maybe you had seen the press release, Mr. Wladimiroff, before us, but I can see it, so ----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The Defence will not rely on hearsay evidence on that matter!

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Of course, you have been very good about helping me with things, but we will have an initial appearance on Tuesday, so we will not begin until 11.30 on Tuesday. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 10 a.m. (The court adjourned until the following day). 23
